chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn Abu al-A'la al-Khaffaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the people were defeated on the Day of Uhud from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he turned towards them with his face while saying: 'I am Muhammad, I am the Messenger of Allah; I have not been killed nor have I died.' So-and-so and so-and-so turned towards him and said: 'Now he is mocking us as well, and we have been defeated.' And with him remained Ali (peace be upon him) and Simak ibn Kharsha, Abu Dujana, may Allah have mercy on him.

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) called him and said: 'O Abu Dujana, leave, and you are free from your pledge of allegiance. As for Ali, I am he and he is me.' So he turned and sat in front of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and wept and said: 'No, by Allah!' And he raised his head to the sky and said: 'No, by Allah! I will not make myself free from my pledge of allegiance. I gave my pledge to you, so where shall I go, O Messenger of Allah? To a wife who dies, or a son who dies, or a house that is ruined, and wealth that perishes, and a term that has drawn near?'

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) showed compassion for him, and he did not cease fighting until he was weighed down by wounds, and he was on one side and Ali (peace be upon him) was on the other side.

So when he was dropped, Ali (peace be upon him) carried him and brought him to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and placed him by his side. So he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, have I fulfilled my pledge?' He said: 'Yes.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said good things to him.

And the people were attacking the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from the right, so Ali (peace be upon him) would repel them. So when he repelled them, the left would come towards the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). That did not cease until his sword broke into three pieces. So he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and threw it in front of him and said: 'This is my sword, it has broken.' So on that day the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) gave him Dh al-Faqar.

And when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saw the trembling of his legs from the abundance of fighting, he raised his head to the sky while weeping and said: 'O Lord, You promised me that You would make Your religion prevail, and if You willed, it would not tire You.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) turned towards the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I hear a loud rumble and I hear the galloping of Hayzoum, and I do not intend to strike anyone except that he falls dead before I strike him.'
He said: 'This is Jibra'il, Mikail, and Isra'il among the angels.'

Then Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came and stood by the side of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad, this is the comfort.' He said: 'Ali is from me and I am from him.' Jibra'il said: 'And I am from both of you.'

Then the people were defeated, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali, go with your sword until you face them. If you see them have mounted the camels and the horses are by their side, then they intend to go to Mecca. And if you see them have mounted the horses and they are leaving the camels by their side, then they intend to go to Medina.'

So Ali (peace be upon him) came to them, and they were upon the camels. So Abu Sufyan said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali, what do you want? That is where we are going, to Mecca. So leave and go to your companion.' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) followed them, and whenever they heard the sound of his horse's hoof, they hastened in their travel, and he kept following them.

So when they moved, they said: 'It is the army of Muhammad which is coming.' Abu Sufyan entered Mecca and informed them of the news. The shepherds and the woodcutters came and entered Mecca and said: 'We saw the army of Muhammad!' Whenever Abu Sufyan moved, a rider on a reddish horse would descend before them, following their tracks. So the people of Mecca came to Abu Sufyan and reproached him.

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) moved, and the flag was with Ali (peace be upon him) and he was in front of him. So when he ascended with the flag from the pass and the people saw him, Ali (peace be upon him) called out: 'O people, this is Muhammad; he has not died and he has not been killed!'

So the companion of the speech who had said, 'He is mocking us and we have been defeated,' said: 'This is Ali, and the flag is in his hand,' until the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) attacked them.

And the women of the Ansar were in their courtyards at the doors of their houses, and the men came out to him, seeking refuge with him and returning to him. And the women, the women of the Ansar, had scratched their faces, spread their hair, cut their forelocks, torn their garments, and tied their bellies for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
So when they saw him, he said good things to them and ordered them to cover themselves and enter their houses.
And he said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He would make His religion prevail over all the religions.'

And Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family): 'Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If then he dies or is killed, will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels, he will by no means do harm to Allah in the least' — the Verse.

key_terms.ذُو الْفَقَارِ: Dh al-Faqar (the famous sword of Ali)

ai.seo_question: What happened to Ali's sword during the Battle of Uhud according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the concept of *al-Walayah* through the Prophet’s declaration 'Ali is from me and I am from him,' linking Ali’s steadfastness directly to the Prophet’s own resilience during the Battle of Uhud. It narrates the miraculous gift of *Dh al-Faqar* and the presence of archangels, culminating in the Prophet’s public reassurance of the Muslims by reciting Surah Ali 'Imran 3:144, thereby affirming that the continuity of the message transcends the Prophet's physical presence.
